candidates.name: Own the verified agent work category
candidates.why: A consistent one-sentence category promise makes mini-ork understandable and retellable during a short GitHub scan.
candidates.first_step: Rewrite README.md:2-28 around one defensible category sentence and a four-noun glossary for recipes, lanes, gates, and certificates.

candidates.name: Proof-first README landing page
candidates.why: A visual hero, trust badges, and a direct action rail make existing mini-ork proof discoverable before a visitor reads implementation detail.
candidates.first_step: Add a See it / Try it / Understand it / Extend it link rail to README.md:2-19.

candidates.name: Canonical install-to-aha path
candidates.why: A short path to a visible result converts a passive star into a firsthand recommendation.
candidates.first_step: Make README.md:202-281 point to one mini-ork demo, starting with a no-provider dry run and optionally continuing to certify-demo.

candidates.name: Named architecture map
candidates.why: A stable diagram and vocabulary let developers place mini-ork in their stack and explain it without reading source.
candidates.first_step: Add a kickoff to recipe to lanes to gates to artifact to learning diagram near README.md:187-200.

candidates.name: Citable why-mini-ork decision surface
candidates.why: A source-backed comparison page supplies the language for an internal adoption decision and differentiates mini-ork from generic orchestration.
candidates.first_step: Link docs/positioning/why-mini-ork.md from the first README screen and add a current use-when / do-not-use-when matrix.

candidates.name: Measured evidence and limits trust bundle
candidates.why: Transparent measurements, failure cases, and safety limits make an agent runtime easier to trust and share.
candidates.first_step: Add an evidence and limits box at README.md:60-80 linking each headline claim to docs/RESULTS.md and docs/SAFETY.md.

candidates.name: Visible release momentum loop
candidates.why: A discoverable release trail gives a GitHub visitor confidence that a star is a useful bookmark for a living project.
candidates.first_step: Add a What is new link and short rolling highlights block near README.md:493-510, sourced from CHANGELOG.md.

candidates.name: Authentic extension and contribution funnel
candidates.why: A curated extension path gives developers a reason to invest in mini-ork and makes future utility visible without moving core scope.
candidates.first_step: Add a maintained recipe/provider gallery entry point to docs/EXTENSION.md:1-18 with contribution and trust boundaries.

candidates.name: Small authentic visual identity
candidates.why: A coherent visual treatment improves recall in the GitHub feed, but only after the proof and category narrative are credible.
candidates.first_step: Define one consistent icon, phrase, and verified-run visual treatment in README.md:2-19 and validate it against the existing screenshot and CLI output.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README.md:8-28 and docs/positioning/why-mini-ork.md:214-217 already state the task-OS and verification thesis.
gap_analysis.gap: The first screen lacks one short category sentence and a stable glossary that compresses the existing primitives.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README.md:12-19 has badges and README.md:30-88 has a demo, results, warning, and IDE screenshot.
gap_analysis.gap: There is no single first-screen action rail routing visitors to proof, trial, architecture, and extension surfaces.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README.md:202-281 documents install, init, kickoff, dry-run, validate, and real-run paths.
gap_analysis.gap: The visitor must choose among several setup paths before reaching a canonical observable aha moment.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README.md:187-200 lists pillars and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md contains the detailed lifecycle.
gap_analysis.gap: A compact visual end-to-end map is missing above the detailed architecture.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: docs/positioning/why-mini-ork.md:1-8 and :34-55 already provide the core comparison thesis.
gap_analysis.gap: The README does not route first-time visitors prominently to a current decision matrix and non-goals.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README.md:60-75 and :469-481 plus docs/RESULTS.md and docs/SAFETY.md already carry measurements and limits.
gap_analysis.gap: Evidence, methodology, safety posture, and status are not packaged together near the hero.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: CHANGELOG.md:1-100 has release and feature history, while README.md:493-503 has a roadmap.
gap_analysis.gap: Release momentum is not a prominent README discovery path or recurring highlights convention.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: docs/EXTENSION.md:1-18 and :26-220 document SDK, workflow, lane, and verifier extension points.
gap_analysis.gap: There is no curated public gallery with maintained examples and a social publishing funnel.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: README.md:2-9 has an icon and tagline, and the existing screenshot supplies some visual language.
gap_analysis.gap: There is no consistent visual system for verified runs, and adding lore before the core story is settled would be premature.

open_questions: Which defensible phrase should mini-ork own for G1: verified agent work, proof-carrying workflows, or another term?
Can a no-provider dry run show meaningful value, or must the canonical G3 path require a real repository and provider?
Which alternatives should the G5 decision page name first, and can every contrast be backed by current docs?
Are the measured results stable enough for G6 hero treatment, or should they remain a linked trust page until refreshed?
Who owns the first maintained gallery and its trust/versioning contract for G8?
Should mini-ork invest in an ork visual language at all, and can it reinforce evidence rather than become mascot theatre?
